fields.headline: Bird flu in the county: questions and answers
fields.intro: Avian influenza was confirmed in one commercial flock. The risk to the public is low. These answers follow federal food safety and public health guidance.

items.q: Is it safe to eat eggs and poultry?
items.a: Yes. Cooking poultry and eggs to the recommended temperature kills the virus. Products from the affected flock do not enter the food supply.
Human infections are rare and have mostly been among people in close contact with infected birds. Workers on the premises are being monitored by the health department.

items.q: I keep backyard chickens. What should I do?
items.a: Keep birds away from wild birds and standing water, wash hands and boots after caring for them, and report sick or dead birds to the hotline.
Supply from the affected flock is lost, and prices may change. The state is working to keep unaffected producers moving product under permit.
